findings.summary: The 'References · [1-9]' assertion cannot become visible in browser preview · the file-input onChange handler awaits `invoke('stash_upload')` which throws in Playwright (no window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__) · the catch block sets `error` and `pending` stays [] · `References · {pending.length}` stays at 'References · 0' forever.
findings.evidence: ThumbnailIdentityUpload.tsx:106-124 · `for (const {file, previewUrl} of previews) { try { const path = await invoke<string>('stash_upload', {...}); setPending(cur => [...cur, {path, name, size, previewUrl}]) } catch (e) { URL.revokeObjectURL(previewUrl); setError(...) } }`. `invoke` (node_modules/@tauri-apps/api/core.js:201-203) calls `window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__.invoke(...)` — undefined in Playwright → TypeError → catch fires → pending never grows → assertion times out at 8000ms.
findings.reproduce: npx playwright test tests/e2e/thumbnail-identity.spec.ts --reporter=list  # expect: timeout waiting for `References · [1-9]`
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) mark this test.fixme with the same follow-up note as url-clip-export / file-drop-export (Tauri invoke shim needed), OR (b) mock `window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__` in addInitScript to short-circuit stash_upload → return synthetic path, OR (c) walk the drop-zone path with `dispatchEvent(new DragEvent(...))` that doesn't route through invoke (won't work · onDrop calls the same onAddFiles). Option (a) is honest with the drift — this really can't be exercised in browser mode until the invoke shim ships.

findings.summary: The `test.fixme`'d URL/file-drop specs still seed ONLY the legacy `app.liquidclips.auth.v1.jwt` key · never the canonical `lc.license.jwt.v1` that getJwt() reads (authStorage.ts:64). When these specs get un-fixme'd (Tauri invoke shim lands), the harness will silently fall through the missing-JWT guard in useMe.ts:190 → snapshot stays null → useTierCaps returns 'clipper' → agency-tier assertions collapse the same way P10/P7/P6 did before this split. Same failure mode, unaddressed.
findings.evidence: grep 'lc.license.jwt.v1' tests/e2e/url-clip-export.spec.ts tests/e2e/file-drop-export.spec.ts → 0 matches. Only 'app.liquidclips.auth.v1.jwt' present. authStorage.ts:64 `const v = s.getItem(LICENSE_JWT_STORAGE_KEY)` where LICENSE_JWT_STORAGE_KEY = 'lc.license.jwt.v1'.
findings.reproduce: grep -c 'lc.license.jwt.v1' tests/e2e/url-clip-export.spec.ts tests/e2e/file-drop-export.spec.ts  # expected: both non-zero if canonical fix landed
findings.suggested_fix: Add the canonical key seed alongside the legacy one now, even though test.fixme means it doesn't run · same 2-line diff as P10/P7/P6 · prevents the next un-fixme sprint from silently repeating the JWT-null failure.

findings.summary: CampaignShellTestHook does NOT expose the `window.__lc_test_*` seam that its sibling AssetRansomPaywallTestHook added at line 42-52 · so Playwright cannot `waitForFunction` before firing the emit · the P10 spec relies on a 200ms `waitForTimeout` (agency-campaign-syndicate.spec.ts:108) which is a brittle race band-aid. On a slow CI runner (cold Vite compile), the test hook's useEffect can fire AFTER the emit, silently losing the event → the campaign shell never mounts → `postBtn.click({timeout: 6000})` times out. AssetRansomPaywallTestHook fixed this exact race in the same 2026-07-07 batch (comment at line 36-41).
findings.evidence: CampaignShellTestHook.tsx:30 `useEvent('test:open-campaign-shell', ...)` · no useEffect-mounted window function. AssetRansomPaywallTestHook.tsx:42-52 attaches `window.__lc_test_open_ransom_paywall` explicitly so Playwright can `waitForFunction` on it. The pattern was learned and applied to the ransom hook but not to the sibling hook shipped in the same file batch.
findings.reproduce: Race is intermittent · would surface as 'button [name=/post to whop marketplace/i] not found' timeout on cold-start CI runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the AssetRansomPaywallTestHook pattern · add a useEffect that attaches `window.__lc_test_open_campaign_shell` + update P10 spec to `waitForFunction(() => typeof window.__lc_test_open_campaign_shell === 'function')` before firing, then call that function instead of __lcBus.emit. Eliminates the 200ms guess.

findings.summary: Performance SLA uses `expect.soft(elapsed).toBeLessThan(5000)` — a soft assertion for the single number this spec exists to lock. A regression from 500ms to 30000ms would still ship green. The spec's file docstring says 'app shell mounts within 2000ms', the assertion says 5000ms, and the runtime behavior can be anything up to Playwright's global timeout. That's three sources of truth for one contract.
findings.evidence: cold-start-returning.spec.ts:91 `expect.soft(elapsed).toBeLessThan(5000)` · line 13 docstring 'JWT + whop_authorized_at both present → skip LoginScreen → app shell mounts within 2000ms'. Soft assertion never fails the test.
findings.reproduce: Manually flip a shell import to a synchronous 10s sleep · rerun the spec · it will still report PASS despite locked regression.
findings.suggested_fix: Either make it a hard `expect(elapsed).toBeLessThan(N)` at whatever number is truly ship-blocking, OR fully embrace 'this is a canary observation' by writing the number to a receipt file the ship-gate reads (e.g. `docs/perf/cold-start-returning.jsonl`) instead of an assertion at all. The current middle-ground assertion masks regressions.

findings.summary: The `bus.emit('engine:complete', {kind: 'export'})` fired before the fetch mint has no effect · PublishModule filters by slug/idx (PublishModule.tsx:204-205 `if (p.slug !== slug) return; if (typeof p.idx === 'number' && p.idx !== focusedClip.idx) return;`) · the emit lands but nothing subscribes-and-acts on a slug-less event. The mint contract is proven by the explicit `page.evaluate(fetch(...))` below · the emit is dead ceremony that makes the test look richer than it is.
findings.evidence: publish-reward-mint.spec.ts:104 `w.__lcBus?.emit('engine:complete', {kind: 'export'})` fires without slug/idx · PublishModule.tsx:202-207 filters out any event where slug != current or idx != focused.
findings.reproduce: Add a bus.on listener for engine:complete in the spec → observe payload · nothing meaningful downstream.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the emit (it's meaningless) or add a comment noting it's a no-op left in as documentation of the real code path. Otherwise a future reader assumes it drives behavior it doesn't.
